compounds.name: Ibutamoren
compounds.description: An oral growth hormone secretagogue; it is not a SARM.
compounds.mechanism: Ghrelin-receptor agonism stimulates endogenous GH release and raises IGF-I.
compounds.findings: An older-adult trial increased fat-free mass without improving strength or function. Glucose control worsened. A separate hip-fracture trial was stopped for a heart-failure signal.
compounds.limits: Older and medically vulnerable populations differ from healthy users. Lean mass is not proof of functional benefit.
compounds.kinetics: Oral exposure was studied. Duration of hormonal effects is not the same as elimination half-life.
compounds.risks: Appetite, fluid retention, myalgia and impaired glucose regulation were observed; heart-failure concern is population-specific, not a quantified universal risk.
compounds.interactions: Clinical combination data remain limited; glucose-lowering therapy and conditions sensitive to fluid retention require assessment.

adverse.context: Observed in the randomized older-adult study.
adverse.frequency: Mean fasting glucose rose by 5 mg/dL (0.3 mmol/L) in the older-adult trial. This is a laboratory change, not diabetes incidence.

adverse.context: Reported during the older-adult trial; some symptoms were transient.
The elderly hip-fracture study ended early; this does not estimate risk in young healthy adults.

unknowns: Long-term cardiovascular outcomes in healthy users.
Whether body-composition changes produce meaningful functional benefit.

compounds.name: Somatropin
compounds.description: Recombinant GH used for defined clinical indications, with substantial safety monitoring requirements.
compounds.mechanism: Activates GH-receptor signaling and alters IGF-I production, growth and metabolism.
compounds.findings: Replacement research and labeling concern diagnosed disorders. In separate critical-illness trials, pharmacologic GH treatment increased mortality.
compounds.limits: Critical-illness findings must not be conflated with properly indicated replacement, and replacement data do not establish enhancement safety.
compounds.kinetics: Formulation and route determine exposure; endocrine effects outlast a simple blood concentration measurement.
compounds.risks: Fluid retention, musculoskeletal symptoms and impaired glucose tolerance are labeled risks. Active malignancy and acute critical illness are important contraindication contexts.
compounds.interactions: Glucocorticoids, glucose-lowering medicines and thyroid replacement may require clinical reassessment.

adverse.context: Recognized particularly in adult replacement therapy.
Treatment can unmask abnormal glucose regulation.

adverse.effect: Increased mortality in acute critical illness
adverse.context: Demonstrated in hospitalized critically ill adults receiving pharmacologic GH.

unknowns: Safety of nonmedical exposure cannot be inferred from replacement practice.
Individual risks depend strongly on underlying disease.

compounds.name: Tesamorelin
compounds.description: A GHRH analogue studied for excess visceral fat in adults with HIV-associated lipodystrophy.
compounds.mechanism: Stimulates pituitary GH secretion and increases IGF-I.
compounds.findings: A randomized trial reduced visceral adiposity in adults with HIV and abdominal fat accumulation.
compounds.limits: This clinical indication does not establish general-purpose weight-loss or bodybuilding benefit.
compounds.kinetics: Formulations differ; product-specific pharmacokinetics and preparation are not interchangeable.
compounds.risks: Labeling identifies hyperglycemia, edema, joint symptoms, hypersensitivity and injection reactions. Prolonged elevated IGF-I has unresolved consequences.
compounds.interactions: GH-mediated changes can affect CYP-metabolized drugs; glucocorticoid replacement and diabetes therapy need review.

adverse.context: Diabetes developed more often than with placebo in the clinical program.
Fluid-retention reactions are recognized.
Rash, urticaria and local reactions occurred in trials.
Active malignancy is a contraindication; this is not proof that treatment causes cancer.

unknowns: Effects of persistently elevated IGF-I over long periods.
Benefits and harms outside the studied indication.

compounds.name: Sermorelin
compounds.description: A short GHRH analogue historically studied in pediatric growth hormone deficiency.
compounds.mechanism: Stimulates GH release from responsive pituitary tissue.
compounds.findings: An open-label pediatric study examined growth during one year of treatment; it did not test healthy-adult longevity or performance.
compounds.limits: Historical pediatric efficacy and diagnostic use do not validate modern anti-aging claims.
compounds.kinetics: A short peptide whose kinetics depend on route. GH responses should not be treated as evidence of sustained clinical benefit.
compounds.risks: Published historical clinical experience does not supply a complete risk estimate for contemporary adult use.
compounds.interactions: Interactions and endocrine effects in current adult combination regimens are inadequately characterized.

adverse.context: Reported in historical clinical review; contemporary adult incidence is uncertain.
Pediatric and diagnostic data do not quantify risks of adult nonmedical exposure.

unknowns: Controlled adult outcome and safety studies for claimed anti-aging use.
Current product identity and formulation equivalence.

compounds.name: CJC-1295
compounds.description: A long-acting GHRH analogue with small human hormonal-response trials.
compounds.mechanism: The studied albumin-binding form prolongs GHRH-like stimulation of GH and IGF-I.
compounds.findings: Early placebo-controlled trials showed sustained hormone increases; they were not trials of muscle gain, healing or longevity.
compounds.limits: Products called “CJC-1295 without DAC” cannot automatically inherit results for the studied long-acting molecule.
compounds.kinetics: The studied DAC form had multi-day persistence. Variant identity is essential when interpreting pharmacokinetics.
compounds.risks: Limited trials cannot exclude rare harms. Compound-specific regulatory safety signals are listed below.
compounds.interactions: Reliable clinical interaction studies are lacking.

adverse.context: FDA describes serious associated events; available clinical evidence is limited.
Repeated administration prolonged IGF-I elevation; long-term outcomes were not established.

unknowns: Long-term cardiovascular and metabolic outcomes.
Equivalence of DAC and non-DAC products.

compounds.name: Ipamorelin
compounds.description: A ghrelin-receptor agonist tested in a small postoperative gastrointestinal trial.
compounds.mechanism: Receptor stimulation can alter GI motility and GH signaling.
compounds.findings: A placebo-controlled bowel-resection study did not show a statistically significant benefit on its key meal-tolerance endpoint.
compounds.limits: Postoperative short-term intravenous data do not establish chronic endocrine or performance safety.
compounds.kinetics: The clinical trial used a specific intravenous formulation; findings do not validate other routes.
compounds.risks: Adverse events in surgical patients require interpretation against a high background event rate; broad safety claims are unwarranted.
compounds.interactions: Clinical interaction evidence for chronic nonmedical use is inadequate.

adverse.context: FDA notes events during intravenous GI-motility research; reporting does not by itself establish causation.
Safety evidence for those exposures is insufficient.

unknowns: Long-term safety with repeated endocrine use.
Route-specific risks and rare-event incidence.

compounds.name: GHRP-2
compounds.description: A peptide secretagogue investigated in small appetite and endocrine experiments.
compounds.mechanism: Ghrelin-receptor agonism stimulates GH; effects are not confined to GH secretion.
compounds.findings: A small crossover experiment found increased food intake. Other endocrine experiments measured prolactin, ACTH and cortisol responses.
compounds.limits: These experiments do not establish long-term functional benefits or a comprehensive safety profile.
compounds.kinetics: Study exposure was route-specific and short; biomarker responses are not a validated chronic regimen.
compounds.risks: Appetite and other pituitary-adrenal hormone changes are documented; serious reports have unresolved causality.
compounds.interactions: Interaction studies for nonmedical combinations are insufficient.

adverse.context: Observed acutely in a small healthy-male study.
Measured after experimental administration; clinical consequences remain uncertain.
FDA lists pancreatitis, infection and deaths; causality was not established.

unknowns: Chronic metabolic effects and clinical outcome benefit.
Reliable compound-specific adverse-event rates.

compounds.name: GHRP-6
compounds.description: A peptide GH secretagogue with small human endocrine and pharmacokinetic studies.
compounds.mechanism: Activates secretagogue signaling and can stimulate additional pituitary-adrenal hormones.
compounds.findings: A nine-person study characterized intravenous kinetics. A separate experiment observed GH, ACTH and cortisol changes.
compounds.limits: Small mechanistic studies cannot determine rare harms or validate recovery and enhancement claims.
compounds.kinetics: The cited intravenous study found biphasic disposition; this does not establish exposure after other routes.
compounds.risks: Clinical long-term safety is poorly characterized; hormonal activity is broader than a selective GH effect.
compounds.interactions: Validated interaction data for chronic combinations are lacking.

adverse.context: Observed in a small human experiment during sleep.
The PK sample and acute experiments cannot quantify repeated-use metabolic or cardiovascular risk.

unknowns: Long-term metabolic and cardiovascular outcomes.
Safety and exposure for marketed non-IV formulations.

compounds.name: Hexarelin
compounds.description: A synthetic GH-releasing peptide examined in small endocrine studies.
compounds.mechanism: Secretagogue signaling stimulates GH and can also affect prolactin and the ACTH–cortisol axis.
compounds.findings: Human experiments documented endocrine responses. A small longer study examined the pituitary-adrenal axis during repeated exposure.
compounds.limits: Biomarker experiments do not prove cardiovascular protection, muscle benefit or long-term safety.
compounds.kinetics: Acute and repeated-exposure endocrine responses can differ; no universal exposure estimate follows.
compounds.risks: The endocrine effects are not GH-specific. Their clinical consequences and chronic adverse-event incidence remain uncertain.
compounds.interactions: Clinical interaction evidence is limited, particularly with other endocrine-active agents.

adverse.context: Measured in human endocrine experiments.
A small clinical study cannot establish rare-event or extended-use safety.

unknowns: Clinically meaningful long-term benefits and harms.
Whether endocrine adaptation predicts clinical outcomes.

compounds.name: BPC-157
compounds.description: An investigational peptide with extensive animal work but very limited human evidence.
compounds.mechanism: Preclinical studies implicate angiogenic and cell-survival signaling; no validated clinical healing mechanism has been established.
compounds.findings: A 2026 systematic review found only three small human studies with 30 participants and very-low-certainty evidence.
compounds.limits: Uncontrolled reports and a two-person safety pilot cannot establish efficacy, uncommon harms or long-term safety.
compounds.kinetics: Human pharmacokinetics remain inadequately characterized for claimed clinical uses.
compounds.risks: No adverse events in tiny reports is not evidence of safety. Product quality and immune reactions remain concerns.

adverse.effect: Rare or delayed adverse effects unknown
adverse.context: The human studies are too small and methodologically weak to characterize them.
FDA identifies potential peptide-product risks; incidence is not established.

adverse.effect: Angiogenic signaling is not clinical cancer proof
adverse.context: VEGFR2-associated effects were studied preclinically; human tumor effects remain unresolved.

unknowns: Controlled human healing efficacy.
Long-term cancer, reproductive and immune safety.

compounds.name: TB-500
compounds.description: A seven-amino-acid fragment often confused with full-length thymosin beta-4.
compounds.mechanism: Biological equivalence to the 43-residue parent peptide has not been demonstrated.
compounds.findings: A 2026 clinical review and FDA evaluation distinguish TB-500 from thymosin beta-4 and identify major evidence gaps.
compounds.limits: Human studies of full-length thymosin beta-4 cannot be relabeled as TB-500 safety or efficacy evidence.
compounds.kinetics: FDA found no clinical pharmacokinetic studies for the evaluated TB-500 forms.
compounds.risks: Human adverse-effect rates are unknown; absence of reports cannot demonstrate safety.
compounds.interactions: No reliable clinical interaction evidence was identified in the evaluated record.

adverse.context: FDA did not identify clinical human safety studies for the evaluated forms.
The FDA evaluation lacked corresponding toxicology studies; this is uncertainty, not a demonstrated harm.
Commercial naming may conflate fragments, parent peptides and derivatives.

unknowns: Whether marketed products contain the evaluated fragment.
Human efficacy, pharmacokinetics and short- or long-term toxicity.

compounds.name: AOD-9604
compounds.description: A modified growth-hormone fragment investigated for obesity-related metabolic effects.
compounds.mechanism: Designed to investigate GH-fragment metabolic activity without simply reproducing full-length GH signaling.
compounds.findings: A pooled report summarized six human trials; its tolerability findings do not establish meaningful weight-loss efficacy.
compounds.limits: Historical oral and intravenous research does not validate contemporary injectable products or every claimed route.
compounds.kinetics: Formulation and route differences prevent a single exposure claim across products.
compounds.risks: Limited historical tolerability data coexist with regulatory uncertainty about product-specific harms.
compounds.interactions: Reliable clinical interaction information is incomplete.

adverse.context: Reported in the clinical safety analysis; treatment attribution was not uniformly established.
FDA notes associated reports; a causal relationship is unclear.
Historical study findings do not establish all current injectable formulations as equivalent.

unknowns: Reproducible clinically meaningful efficacy.
Route-specific immunogenicity and longer-term safety.

compounds.name: GW501516
compounds.description: A PPARδ agonist with human lipid studies and serious preclinical safety concerns; it is not a SARM.
compounds.mechanism: Activates a nuclear receptor controlling lipid-related gene expression.
compounds.findings: A randomized study changed lipoprotein markers in people with low HDL. It did not demonstrate improved clinical cardiovascular outcomes.
compounds.limits: Favorable lipid biomarkers do not resolve carcinogenicity concerns or establish endurance-use safety.
compounds.kinetics: Oral clinical exposure was investigated; pharmacokinetics do not supply evidence of acceptable long-term risk.
compounds.risks: Regulators report animal-cancer findings; the corresponding magnitude of human cancer risk is unknown.
compounds.interactions: Clinical interaction information is insufficient for nonmedical use.

adverse.context: HSA reports cancers in animal studies; this does not quantify human incidence.
WADA issued an alert about preclinical toxicities and discontinued development.
Short lipid trials cannot exclude cancer or rare delayed toxicity.

unknowns: Human long-term cancer risk.
Clinical outcome benefit despite lipid-marker changes.

compounds.name: SR9009
compounds.description: A research compound often marketed using an oversimplified REV-ERB mechanism.
compounds.mechanism: Although described as a REV-ERB agonist, genetic experiments found important effects persisting without REV-ERB receptors.
compounds.findings: Cell experiments demonstrated altered proliferation, metabolism and gene expression independent of the nominal target.
compounds.limits: This undermines treating every SR9009 effect as a specific REV-ERB effect; it does not establish human efficacy.
compounds.kinetics: Human absorption and exposure are not established by the cited cell and genetic-model work.
compounds.risks: Human clinical adverse effects are poorly characterized; cellular effects should not be presented as a clinical safety profile.

adverse.context: Observed experimentally, including when REV-ERBs were absent; human relevance is uncertain.
No validated human risk estimate follows from the cited study.

unknowns: Clinically relevant molecular targets.
Human efficacy, bioavailability and toxicity.

compounds.name: SLU-PP-332
compounds.description: A small-molecule ERR agonist investigated as an exercise mimetic in preclinical models.
compounds.mechanism: Activates ERR-dependent metabolic transcription; estrogen-related receptors are distinct from estrogen receptors.
compounds.findings: Mouse and cell studies found oxidative-muscle and endurance-related changes. Newer studies examine scaffold chemistry and in vitro metabolism.
compounds.limits: Mouse endurance gains do not establish human benefit, absorption or safety.
compounds.kinetics: Human liver-system experiments identify metabolites but are not human clinical pharmacokinetic trials.
compounds.risks: Human clinical adverse-effect rates are not established by this preclinical evidence.

adverse.context: The cited efficacy foundation is preclinical, not a human safety program.
In vitro metabolic characterization does not establish the clinical effects of metabolites.

unknowns: Human exposure and efficacy.
Long-term organ, reproductive and cardiovascular safety.

compounds.name: Semaglutide
compounds.description: A GLP-1 receptor agonist with large clinical programs; indications and risks depend on the product.
compounds.mechanism: Alters glucose-dependent insulin signaling, glucagon release, appetite and gastric emptying.
compounds.findings: STEP 1 demonstrated substantial weight reduction in adults with overweight or obesity; clinical context matters.
compounds.limits: Trial products and monitored populations cannot be treated as equivalent to unverified products.
compounds.kinetics: Injectable and oral formulations have distinct absorption properties; product names are not interchangeable formulations.
compounds.risks: GI adverse effects are common. Labels also address pancreatitis, gallbladder disease, dehydration-related kidney injury and other serious risks.
compounds.interactions: Insulin or secretagogues can increase hypoglycemia risk; delayed gastric emptying can affect oral-drug assessment.

adverse.context: Frequent clinical-trial and labeled adverse reactions.
Recognized label warnings; individual causality and incidence depend on the event and population.
Renal injury can accompany fluid loss; hypoglycemia risk rises with insulin or secretagogues.
Boxed warning; whether this translates to human medullary thyroid carcinoma is unknown.

unknowns: Individualized risk in underrepresented populations.
Unverified products cannot inherit pharmaceutical trial safety.

compounds.name: Tirzepatide
compounds.description: A dual incretin-receptor agonist studied in diabetes, obesity and related clinical conditions.
compounds.mechanism: Activates GIP and GLP-1 receptors, affecting appetite, insulin secretion and gastric emptying.
compounds.findings: SURMOUNT-1 demonstrated substantial weight reduction in adults with obesity; GI events were the most common adverse events.
compounds.limits: Comparisons with other drugs require comparable populations, estimands and trial designs.
compounds.kinetics: Prolonged exposure and delayed gastric emptying are relevant; clinical product information is formulation-specific.
compounds.risks: Common GI reactions coexist with labeled pancreatitis, gallbladder, dehydration, hypersensitivity and hypoglycemia warnings.
compounds.interactions: Can alter oral-drug absorption; oral hormonal contraception and insulin/secretagogue therapy require specific clinical review.

adverse.context: GI symptoms dominate the clinical adverse-event profile and can be severe.
Label warnings require clinical interpretation rather than assuming every abdominal symptom has one cause.

adverse.effect: Kidney injury with volume depletion / hypoglycemia context
adverse.context: Fluid loss and concurrent glucose-lowering treatments modify risk.
Boxed warning; human relevance remains undetermined.

unknowns: Long-term risk estimates continue to evolve.
Safety cannot be transferred to unverified or differently formulated products.

compounds.name: Retatrutide
compounds.description: An investigational triple agonist with published phase 3 evidence as of 2026.
compounds.mechanism: Activates three hormone receptors involved in energy and glucose regulation.
compounds.findings: TRIUMPH-1 and TRIUMPH-2 report weight reduction; the latter studied adults with obesity and type 2 diabetes.
compounds.limits: Phase 3 efficacy does not equal marketing approval or establish equivalence of products sold outside trials.
compounds.kinetics: The clinical program studies a specific long-acting formulation; unverified products cannot inherit its exposure profile.
compounds.risks: GI effects, heart-rate changes, hypotension and altered sensation have been reported in the clinical program.
compounds.interactions: Comprehensive interaction information remains under development; there is no approved prescribing label for general use.

adverse.context: Nausea and diarrhea were more common than placebo in TRIUMPH-2.
adverse.frequency: TRIUMPH-2: nausea 14–28% versus 8% with placebo; diarrhea 27–34% versus 13%. Rates varied across study arms.

adverse.context: Dose-related increases occurred in the earlier phase 2 obesity trial.
More frequent than placebo in the 2026 diabetes/obesity phase 3 trial.
Approval has not been granted; ongoing research continues to define the risk-benefit profile.

unknowns: Rare adverse-event and long-term outcome estimates.
Interactions and safety beyond studied populations.
